questions.q: Tangents are drawn from the point $\left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ to the hyperbola $3{x}^{2} - 2{y}^{2} = 6$ and are inclined at angles $\theta and ϕ$ to the $x$-axis. If $\left(tan ⁡ \theta\right)\left(tan ⁡ ϕ\right) = 2$, then the value of $2{\alpha}^{2} - {\beta}^{2}$ is
questions.solution:
Given hyperbola is 3{x}^{2} - 2{y}^{2} = 6 or $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{3} = 1$
Slope form of tangent is $y = mx \pm \sqrt{{a}^{2}{m}^{2} - {b}^{2}}$or ${\left(y - mx\right)}^{2} = {a}^{2}{m}^{2} - {b}^{2}$

Tangent from the point $\left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ is given by,

${\left(\beta - m\alpha\right)}^{2} = 2{m}^{2} - 3$
$⇒ {m}^{2}\left({\alpha}^{2} - 2\right) - 2\alpha\betam + {\beta}^{2} + 3 = 0$
${m}_{1}{m}_{2} = \dfrac{{\beta}^{2} + 3}{{\alpha}^{2} - 2} = 2 = tan ⁡ \thetatan ⁡ ϕ$
$∴ {\beta}^{2} + 3 = 2{\alpha}^{2} - 4 ⇒ 7 = 2{\alpha}^{2} - {\beta}^{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If two points $P$ and $Q$ lie on the hyperbola $\dfrac{x2}{a2} - \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1 ( a < b )$, whose centre $C$ be such that $CP$ is perpendicular to $CQ$, then the value of $\dfrac{1}{CP^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{CQ^{2}}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $CP = {r}_{1}$ be inclined to transverse axis at an angle $\theta$ such that $P \left({r}_{1}$cos ⁡ $\theta, {r}_{1}$ sin ⁡ $\theta\right) lies on$ the hyperbola. Therefore,

{r}_{1}^{2}$\left(\dfrac{{cos}^{2} ⁡ \theta}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{{sin}^{2} ⁡ \theta}{b^{2}}\right) =1$

Replacing $\thetaby{90}^{o} + $\theta, we get,

${r}_{2}^{2}\left(\dfrac{{sin}^{2} ⁡ \theta}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{{cos}^{2} ⁡ \theta}{b^{2}}\right) =1$

(where, $CQ = {r}_{2}$)

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{{r}_{1}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{r}_{2}^{2}} = \dfrac{{cos}^{2} ⁡ \theta}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{{sin}^{2} ⁡ \theta}{b^{2}} + \dfrac{{sin}^{2} ⁡ \theta}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{{cos}^{2} ⁡ \theta}{b^{2}}

$⇒ 1{r}_{1}^{2} + 1{r}_{2}^{2} = {cos}^{2} ⁡ $\theta \left(\dfrac{1}{a2} - \dfrac{1}{b2}\right) + {sin}^{2}$⁡ $\theta\left(\dfrac{1}{a2} - \dfrac{1}{b2}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{{r}_{1}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{r}_{2}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{b^{2}}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{CP^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{CQ^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{b^{2}}$

questions.q: If a circle drawn by assuming a chord parallel to the transverse axis of hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1$ as diameter always passes through $\left(2,0\right)$, then
questions.solution:
Let, the end points of the diameter of circle are $\left(asec ⁡ \theta, btan ⁡ \theta\right)$ & $\left(- asec ⁡ \theta,btan ⁡ \theta\right)$
$⇒$ Equation of circle is $\left(x - asec ⁡ \theta\right)\left(x + asec ⁡ \theta\right) + {\left(y - btan ⁡ \theta\right)}^{2} = 0$
$⇒ x^{2} - a^{2}{sec}^{2} ⁡ \theta + y^{2} + b^{2}{tan}^{2} ⁡ \theta - 2btan ⁡ \thetay = 0$
Because $\left(2,0\right)$ satisfies above equation,
hence,~$4 - a^{2}\left(1 + {tan}^{2} ⁡ \theta\right) + 0 + b^{2}{tan}^{2} ⁡ \theta = 0$
$⇒ \left(4 - a^{2}\right) + \left(b^{2} - a^{2}\right){tan}^{2} ⁡ \theta = 0$
Which is always true if $\left|a\right| = 2$ & $\left|b\right| = 2$

questions.q: From a point $P,$ two tangents $PA$ and $PB$ are drawn to the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1 .$ If these tangents cut the coordinate axes at $4$ concyclic points, then the locus of $P$ is&
questions.solution:
Let the equation of tangents are
$y = {m}_{1}x + {C}_{1},$ and
$y = {m}_{2}x + {C}_{2}$
which cuts the coordinate axes at $E, F, G, H$ as shown in the figure
Now, $OE \times OG = OF \times OH$
$⇒ \left(\dfrac{- {C}_{1}}{{m}_{1}}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{+ {C}_{2}}{{m}_{2}}\right) = \left({C}_{1}\right)\left(- {C}_{2}\right)⇒ {m}_{1}{m}_{2} = 1$
Let $P$ be $\left(h, k\right)$ and equation of the tangent through $P$ on the hyperbola is
$y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^{2}m^{2} - b^{2}}$
$⇒ { \left(k^{2} - mh\right)$}^{2} = $\left(a^{2}m^{2} - b^{2}\right)$
$⇒ \left(h^{2} - a^{2}\right)m^{2} - 2khm + k^{2} + b^{2} = 0$
whose roots are {m}_{1} and ${m}_{2} ⇒ {m}_{1}{m}_{2} = \dfrac{k^{2} + b^{2}}{h^{2} - a^{2}} =$1$
$⇒$ locus is $x^{2} - y^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}

questions.q: For the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1,$ distance between the foci is $10$~units. From the point $\left(2, \sqrt{3}\right),$ perpendicular tangents are drawn to the hyperbola, then the value of $\left|\dfrac{b}{a}\right|$ is
questions.solution:
Let,& $e$ be the eccentricity of the hyperbola
Now,~$2ae = 10 ⇒ a^{2}e^{2} = 25$
$⇒ a^{2} + b^{2} = 25$
Also $\left(2, \sqrt{3}\right)$ lies on the director circle~$x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2} - b^{2}$
$⇒ 7 = a^{2} - b^{2} ⇒ a^{2} = 16, b^{2} = 9$
$⇒ \left|\dfrac{b}{a}\right| = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0 . 75$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A tangent drawn to the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1$ at $P \left($asec ⁡ $\dfrac{π}{6},$btan ⁡ $\dfrac{π}{6}\right) form a triangle of area $3a^{2}$ sq. units with the coordinate axes. The eccentricity of the conjugate hyperbola of \dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} =$1$ is$
questions.solution:
$P = \left(\dfrac{2a}{\sqrt{3}}, \dfrac{b}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$
Equation of the tangent at $P$ is $\dfrac{2x}{\sqrt{3}a} - \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{3}b} = 1$
$x$ intercept & $y$ intercept of the tangent are $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}a}{2}$ & $- \sqrt{3}b$ respectively
Area of the triangle formed by the tangent with the coordinate axes is 
$\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}a}{2} \times \sqrt{3}b = 3{a}^{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{b}{a} = 4 ⇒ \dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{1}{4}$
The eccentricity of the conjugate hyperbola equals to
$\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1}{16}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The locus of the mid-point of the chords of the hyperbola $x^{2} - y^{2} = 4,$ that touches the parabola $y^{2} = 8x$ is
questions.solution:
Let midpoint of the chord be $P\left(h, k\right) .$

Then, the equation of the chord will be $xh - yk = h^{2} - k^{2}$
$⇒ y = \dfrac{h}{k}x + \dfrac{k^{2} - h^{2}}{k}$ … $\left(1\right)$
Now, the line $y = mx + c$ is tangent to $y^{2} = 4ax$ if $c = \dfrac{a}{m}$
Hence, equation $\left(1\right)$ is tangent to $y^{2} = 8x$ if
$\dfrac{k^{2} - h^{2}}{k} = \dfrac{2k}{h} ⇒ y^{2}x - x^{3} = 2y^{2}$
$⇒ y^{2}\left(x - 2\right) = x^{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The locus of the mid-points of the chords of the hyperbola $3x^{2} - 2y^{2} + 4x - 6y = 0$ which are parallel to the line $y = 2x + 4$& is
questions.solution:
Let mid-point of the chord is $\left(h, k\right)$
$⇒$ equation of the chord is
$3hx - 2ky + 4\left(\dfrac{x + h}{2}\right) - 6\left(\dfrac{y + k}{2}\right) = 3h^{2} - 2k^{2} + 4h - 6k$
$⇒ \left(3h + 2\right)x + \left(- 2k - 3\right)y = 3h^{2} - 2k^{2} + 2h - 3k$
$⇒$ Slope of the chord is equal to $\dfrac{3h + 2}{2k + 3} = 2$
$⇒$ locus of the mid-points is $3x + 2 = 4y + 6$
$⇒ 3x - 4y - 4 = 0$

questions.q: The chords passing through $\left(2,1\right)$ intersect the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{16} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{9} = 1$ at $A and B .$ The locus of the point of intersection of tangents at $A and B$ on the hyperbola is
questions.solution:
Let, the point of intersection of the tangents at A$ & $B$ is \left(h, k\right) .
Then,$ the equation ofAB$ is \dfrac{xh}{16} - \dfrac{yk}{9} =1$ { $∵ T = 0$ is the chord of contact}
Now,~$\dfrac{xh}{16} - \dfrac{yk}{9} =$1$ passes through \left(2,1\right)
Hence,~\dfrac{2h}{16} - \dfrac{k}{9} =1$
$⇒ 9h - 8k = 72$
$⇒$~the locus is $9x - 8y = 72$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two straight lines having variable slopes ${m}_{1}$~and& ${m}_{2}$ pass through the fixed points~$\left(a, 0\right)$~and& $\left(- a, 0\right)$ respectively. If ${m}_{1}{m}_{2} = 2$, then the eccentricity of the locus of the point of intersection of the lines is
questions.solution:
Let, the lines are $y = {m}_{1} \left(x - a\right)$ and $y = {m}_{2} \left(x + a\right)$

which intersects at the point $\left(h, k\right) .$

$⇒ k = {m}_{1}\left(h - a\right)$ & $k = {m}_{2} \left($ h + a\right)$

$⇒ k^{2} = {m}_{1}{m}_{2} $\left($ h^{2} - a^{2}\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{k^{2}}{2} = h^{2} - a^{2}$ (given,& ${m}_{1}{m}_{2} = 2$)

$⇒ \dfrac{x^{2}}{1} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{2} = a^{2}$ (Hyperbola)

Eccentricity $= \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{2}{1}} = \sqrt{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The sum of the $y$-intercepts of the tangents drawn from the point $\left(- 2, - 1\right)$ to the hyperbola $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{3} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{2} = 1$ is
questions.solution:
Let, the equation of the tangent from $\left(- 2, - 1\right)$ is $y = mx + \sqrt{3{m}^{2} - 2}$
$⇒ - 1 = - 2m + \sqrt{3{m}^{2} - 2}$
$⇒ {\left(2m - 1\right)}^{2} = 3{m}^{2} - 2$
$⇒ {m}^{2} - 4m + 3 = 0$
$⇒ m = 1, 3$
So, the equations of the tangents are
$\left(y + 1\right) = \left(x + 2\right) \text{ and } \left(y + 1\right) = 3\left(x + 2\right)$
$⇒ y$-intercepts of the tangents are $1$ & $5$
$⇒$ the sum of $y$-intercepts $= 6$
questions.question: The sum of the $y$-intercepts of the tangents drawn from the point $\left(- 2, - 1\right)$ to the hyperbola $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{3} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{2} = 1$ is
questions.explanation:
Let, the equation of the tangent from $\left(- 2, - 1\right)$ is $y = mx + \sqrt{3{m}^{2} - 2}$
$⇒ - 1 = - 2m + \sqrt{3{m}^{2} - 2}$
$⇒ {\left(2m - 1\right)}^{2} = 3{m}^{2} - 2$
$⇒ {m}^{2} - 4m + 3 = 0$
$⇒ m = 1, 3$
So, the equations of the tangents are
$\left(y + 1\right) = \left(x + 2\right) \text{ and } \left(y + 1\right) = 3\left(x + 2\right)$
$⇒ y$-intercepts of the tangents are $1$ & $5$
$⇒$ the sum of $y$-intercepts $= 6$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The locus of a point which moves such that the difference of its distances from the points $\left(5,0\right)$ and $\left(- 5,0\right)$ is $6$& units is a conic, whose length of the latus rectum (in units) is equal to
questions.solution:
Because& $6 < 5 - \left(-5\right)
Hence,$ the locus is a hyperbola by definition.
Let's assume the eccentricity, semi-transverse axis and the semi-conjugate axis of the hyperbola ise, a, and b$ respectively, then

$2ae = 10$ {Distance between focii \left(-5,0\right) & \left(5,0\right) = 10 = 2ae$ }
& $2a = 6 ⇒ e = \dfrac{10}{6} = \dfrac{5}{3}$
$⇒ 1 + \dfrac{b^{2}}{a^{2}} =$ e^{2} = $\dfrac{25}{9}⇒ \dfrac{b^{2}}{a^{2}} = \dfrac{25}{9} -$1 = $\dfrac{16}{9}$
$⇒ \dfrac{2b^{2}}{a} =2 \times \dfrac{16}{9}$ \timesa = $\dfrac{32}{3}=length$ of the latus rectum

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the line $y = x + c$ touches the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{9} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{5} = 1$ at the point $P   \left(h, k\right), then  \left(h, k\right) can be equal to$
questions.solution:
Tangent at $P\left(h, k\right)$ is $\dfrac{hx}{9} - \dfrac{ky}{5} = 1$ which is same as $y = x + c$ (where $c = \pm \sqrt{9\left(1\right) - 5} = \pm 2$ )
$⇒ \dfrac{hx}{9} - \dfrac{ky}{5} - 1 = 0$ and $x - y \pm 2 = 0$ are identical
$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{h}{9}}{1} = \dfrac{- \dfrac{k}{5}}{- 1} = \dfrac{- 1}{\pm 2}$
$⇒ \left(h, k\right) = \left(- \dfrac{9}{2}, - \dfrac{5}{2}\right)or\left(\dfrac{9}{2}, \dfrac{5}{2}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area (in sq. units) of the triangle formed by the lines $y = 2x, y = - 2x$ and the tangent at the point $\left(\sqrt{5}, 4\right)$ on $4x^{2} - y^{2} = 4$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Equation of the tangent at point $\left(\sqrt{5}, 4\right)$ on $4x^{2} - y^{2} = 4$ is $4x\sqrt{5} - 4y = 4 ⇒ \sqrt{5}x - y = 1$.
Now, point of intersection of $y = \sqrt{5}x - 1 & y = 2x$ is $\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5} - 2}, \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5} - 2}\right)$.
Point of intersection of $y = \sqrt{5}x - 1$ and $y = - 2x$ is& $\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5} + 2}, \dfrac{- 2}{\sqrt{5} + 2}\right) .$
Point of intersection of $y = 2x$ & $y = - 2x$ is $\left(0,0\right)$
Now, area of the triangle formed by the points $\left(0,0\right), \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5} - 2}, \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5} - 2}\right), \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5} + 2}, \dfrac{- 2}{\sqrt{5} + 2}\right)
$= $\left|\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1\left(\sqrt{5} -2\right) & 2\left(\sqrt{5} -2\right) & 1 \\ 1\left(\sqrt{5} +2\right) & - 2\left(\sqrt{5} +2\right) & 1\end{cases}\right|\right| = \left|\dfrac{1}{2} \times1 \times \left(-2 - 2\right)\right| = 2$& sq.units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let the eccentricity of the hyperbola with the principal axes along the coordinate axes and passing through $\left(3,0\right)$ and $\left(3\sqrt{2}, 2\right)$ is $e$, then the value of $\left(\dfrac{{e}^{2} + 1}{{e}^{2} - 1}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
One vertex of the hyperbola is $\left(3,0\right) .$

So, assuming the equation of hyperbola as $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$
and passing through $\left(3\sqrt{2}, 2\right)$, we get,
$⇒ \dfrac{9\left(2\right)}{9} - \dfrac{4}{{b}^{2}} = 1 ⇒ 1 = \dfrac{4}{{b}^{2}} ⇒ {b}^{2} = 4$
$⇒ {e}^{2} = 1 + \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} = 1 + \dfrac{4}{9} = \dfrac{13}{9}$
$⇒ \dfrac{{e}^{2} + 1}{{e}^{2} - 1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{13}{9} + 1}{\dfrac{13}{9} - 1} = \dfrac{22}{4} = \dfrac{11}{2} = 5 . 5$
questions.question: Let the eccentricity of the hyperbola with the principal axes along the coordinate axes and passing through $\left(3,0\right)$ and $\left(3\sqrt{2}, 2\right)$ is $e$, then the value of $\left(\dfrac{{e}^{2} + 1}{{e}^{2} - 1}\right)$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
One vertex of the hyperbola is $\left(3,0\right) .$

So, assuming the equation of hyperbola as $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$
and passing through $\left(3\sqrt{2}, 2\right)$, we get,
$⇒ \dfrac{9\left(2\right)}{9} - \dfrac{4}{{b}^{2}} = 1 ⇒ 1 = \dfrac{4}{{b}^{2}} ⇒ {b}^{2} = 4$
$⇒ {e}^{2} = 1 + \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} = 1 + \dfrac{4}{9} = \dfrac{13}{9}$
$⇒ \dfrac{{e}^{2} + 1}{{e}^{2} - 1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{13}{9} + 1}{\dfrac{13}{9} - 1} = \dfrac{22}{4} = \dfrac{11}{2} = 5 . 5$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The point of intersection of the tangents drawn to the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1$ at the points where it is intersected by the line $lx + my + n = 0$ is&
questions.solution:
Let,& $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ be the required point. Then, the equation of the chord of contact of the tangents drawn from $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ to the given hyperbola is
$\dfrac{x{x}_{1}}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{y{y}_{1}}{b^{2}} = 1$ …(i)
The given line is $lx + my + n = 0$ …(ii)
Equations (i) and (ii) represent the same line
$∴ \dfrac{{x}_{1}}{a^{2}l} = \dfrac{- {y}_{1}}{b^{2}m} = \dfrac{1}{- n}$
$⇒ {x}_{1} = \dfrac{- a^{2}l}{n}, {y}_{1} = \dfrac{b^{2}m}{n} .
Hence,$ the required point is$\left(- \dfrac{a^{2}l}{n}, \dfrac{b^{2}m}{n}\right)$

questions.q: The locus of the point of intersection of two tangents of the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{4} = 1,$ if the product of their slopes is $1,$& is
questions.solution:
Equation of any tangent of the hyperbola with slope $m$ is $y = mx \pm \sqrt{2m^{2} - 4}$
If it passes through $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ then
$\left({y}_{1} - m{x}_{1}\right)2 = 2m^{2} - 4 ⇒ \left({x}_{1}^{2} - 2\right)m^{2} - 2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}m + \left({y}_{1}^{2} + 4\right) = 0$
If $n = {m}_{1}, {m}_{2}$ then as given ${m}_{1}{m}_{2} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{{y}_{1}^{2} + 4}{{x}_{1}^{2} - 2} = 1$
Hence, the required locus is $y^{2} + 4 = \left(x^{2} - 2\right)$

questions.q: If the eccentricity of the hyperbola $x^{2} - y^{2}\sec^{2} ⁡ \alpha = 5$ is $\sqrt{3} times the eccentricity of the ellipse $x^{2}\sec^{2} ⁡ \alpha + y^{2} = 25,$ then \tan^{2} ⁡ \alpha$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let eccentricity of the hyperbola& $\dfrac{x^{2}}{5} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{5\cos^{2} ⁡ \alpha} = 1$ is
${e}_{1}^{2} = 1 + \dfrac{b^{2}}{a^{2}} = 1 + \dfrac{5\cos^{2} ⁡ \alpha}{5} = 1 + \cos^{2} ⁡ \alpha;$
Similarly, eccentricity of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{25\cos^{2} ⁡ \alpha} + \dfrac{y^{2}}{25} = 1$ is

${e}_{2}^{2} = 1 - \dfrac{25\cos^{2} ⁡ \alpha}{25}= \sin^{2} ⁡ \alpha;$

Putting ${e}_{1} = \sqrt{3}{e}_{2} ⇒ {e}_{1}^{2} = 3{e}_{2}^{2}$
$⇒ 1 + \cos^{2} ⁡ \alpha = 3\sin^{2} ⁡ \alpha ⇒ 2 = 4\sin^{2} ⁡ \alpha$
$⇒ sin ⁡ \alpha = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} ⇒ \tan^{2} ⁡ \alpha = 1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of triangle formed by the lines $x - y = 0, x + y = 0$ and any tangent to the hyperbola $x^{2} - y^{2} = 16$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Equation of the tangent to the hyperbola $x^{2} - y^{2} = 16$ in parametric form is
$4xsec ⁡ ϕ - 4ytan ⁡ ϕ = 16$
$⇒ xsec ⁡ ϕ - ytan ⁡ ϕ = 4$
Solving with $y = x and y = - x$, we get,
$A\left(4\left(sec ⁡ ϕ + tan ⁡ ϕ\right), 4\left(sec ⁡ ϕ + tan ⁡ ϕ\right)\right),$
$B \left(4 \left(sec ⁡ ϕ - tan ⁡ ϕ\right), $4$\left(tan ⁡ ϕ - sec ⁡ ϕ\right)\right)$
$∴$ Area bounded by $∆ AOB$
$= \left|\dfrac{1}{2}\l$lleft(16$\left(\tan^{2}⁡ ϕ - \sec^{2} ⁡ ϕ\right)$- 16$\left(\sec^{2}⁡ ϕ - \tan^{2} ⁡ ϕ\right)\right)\right|$
$= \left|\dfrac{1}{2}\left(-16 - 16\right)\right| = 16$& sq.& units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The locus of a point $P \left(\alpha, \beta\right) moving under the condition that the line $ y = \alphax + $\beta is a tangent to the hyperbola \dfrac{x^{2}}{1} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} =1$ is a conic, with eccentricity equal to
questions.solution:
The tangent to the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{1} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1$ is $y = mx \pm \sqrt{m^{2} - b^{2}}$
Given that, $y = \alphax + \beta$ is a tangent to the hyperbola.
So, $m = \alpha$ and $m^{2} - b^{2} = {\beta}^{2}$
$∴ {\alpha}^{2} - b^{2} = {\beta}^{2}$
The locus is $x^{2} - y^{2} = b^{2},$ which is a hyperbola having eccentricity $= \sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From a point on the line $x - y + 2 = 0$ tangents are drawn to the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{6} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{2} = 1$ such that the chord of contact passes through a fixed point $\left(\lambda, \mu\right)$. Then,~$\mu - \lambda$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let the point be $\left(\alpha, \beta\right) ⇒ \beta = \alpha + 2$
Chord of contact of the hyperbola is $T = 0$
$⇒ \dfrac{\alphax}{6} - \dfrac{\betay}{2} = 1$
$⇒ \dfrac{\alphax}{6} - \dfrac{\left(\alpha + 2\right)y}{2} = 1$
$⇒ \alpha\left(\dfrac{x}{6} - \dfrac{y}{2}\right) - \left(\dfrac{2y}{2} +1\right) = 0$
Since, this passes through the fixed point $\left(\lambda, \mu\right)$
$∴ \dfrac{\lambda}{6} - \dfrac{\mu}{2} =0$ and $\dfrac{2\mu}{2} +1 = 0$

So, $\mu = - 1$ and $\lambda = - 3$
$⇒ \mu - \lambda = 2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From a point $P,$ two tangents $PA$ and $PB$ are drawn to the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1$. If the product of the slopes of these tangents is $1,$ then the locus of $P$ is a conic whose eccentricity is equal to
questions.solution:
Let, $P$ be $\left(h, k\right)$ and the equation of tangent through $P$ on the hyperbola is
$y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^{2}m^{2} - b^{2}}$
$⇒ { \left(k^{2} - mh\right)$}^{2} =$\left(a^{2}m^{2} - b^{2}\right)$
$⇒ \left(h^{2} - a^{2}\right)m^{2} - 2khm + k^{2} + b^{2} = 0$ where roots are ${m}_{1} and {m}_{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{k^{2} + b^{2}}{h^{2} - a^{2}} =$1 = {m}_{1}{m}_{2}$
$⇒$ locus is $x^{2} - y^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}$
$⇒$ eccentricity $= \sqrt{1 + 1} = \sqrt{2}$

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A hyperbola has foci $\left(4,2\right), \left(2, 2\right)$ and it passes throughP$\left(2, 4\right)$.$& The eccentricity of the hyperbola is$
questions.solution:
Let $\left(4, 2\right) = {S}_{1}$ and $\left(2, 2\right) = {S}_{2}$ and

the eccentricity of the hyperbola is $e$, then

{S}_{1}{S}_{2} = 2ae and $\left|P{S}_{1} - P{S}_{2}\right| = 2a$ (where,~$2a$ is the length of the transverse axis)
$⇒ e = \dfrac{{S}_{1}{S}_{2}}{\left|P{S}_{1} - P{S}_{2}\right|} = \dfrac{2}{2\sqrt{2} - 2}$
$⇒ e = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2} - 1} = \sqrt{2} + 1 = tan ⁡ \dfrac{3\pi}{8}$

questions.q: The locus of the midpoint of the chords of the hyperbola $\dfrac{x2}{25} - \dfrac{y2}{36} = 1$ which passes through the point $\left(2, 4\right)$ is a hyperbola, whose transverse axis length (in units) is equal to
questions.solution:
The equation of the chord whose mid-point is $( h, k )$ is $T = {S}_{1}$
$⇒ \dfrac{xh}{25} - \dfrac{yk}{36} = \dfrac{h2}{25} - \dfrac{k2}{36}$
Since it passes through $\left(2, 4\right)$
$\dfrac{2h}{25} - \dfrac{4k}{36} = \dfrac{h2}{25} - \dfrac{k2}{36} ⇒ \dfrac{h^{2} - 2h + 1}{25} - \dfrac{k^{2} - 4k + 4}{36} = \dfrac{1}{25} - \dfrac{4}{36}$
Hence, the locus of $\left(h, k\right)$ is
$\dfrac{\left(x - 1\right)2}{\dfrac{16}{9}} - \dfrac{\left(y - 2\right)2}{\dfrac{64}{25}} = - 1$
This is the equation of a hyperbola whose transverse axis length is $\dfrac{16}{5}$& units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A hyperbola having the transverse axis of length $\sqrt{2} units has the same focii as that of ellipse 3x^{2} + 4y^{2} = 12$, then its equation is
questions.solution:
For the hyperbola& $\dfrac{x2}{a2} - \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1,$~length of semi transverse axis& $a = \dfrac{1}{2},$

For the ellipse~$\dfrac{x2}{4} + \dfrac{y2}{3} = 1,$~the foci is& $\left(\pm 1,0\right)$

i.e.~$\pm 1 = \pm \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}$

$⇒ b^{2} = 1 - a^{2} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Hence, the equation of the required hyperbola is~$\dfrac{x2}{\dfrac{1}{2}} - \dfrac{y2}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = 1$

questions.q: Let ${C}_{1}$ be the graph of $xy = 1$ and the reflection of ${C}_{1}$ in the line $y = 2x$ is ${C}_{2} .$ If the equation of ${C}_{2}$ is expressed as $12{x}^{2} + bxy + c{y}^{2} + d = 0$, then the value of $( b + c + d )$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Any point on the hyperbola $xy = 1$ is $\left(t, \dfrac{1}{t}\right)$
Now, the image of $\left(t, \dfrac{1}{t}\right)$ by the line mirror $y = 2x$ is
$\dfrac{x - t}{2} = \dfrac{y - \dfrac{1}{t}}{- 1} = - 2\left(\dfrac{2t - \dfrac{1}{t}}{5}\right)$
$⇒ 5x = \dfrac{4}{t} - 3t$ and $5y = 4t + \dfrac{3}{t}$
Now eliminating $t$ from above two equations we get,
$12{x}^{2} - 12{y}^{2} - 7xy + 25 = 0$
$∴ b + c + d = 6$

questions.q: If the eccentricity of the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{{\left(1 + sin ⁡ \theta\right)}^{2}} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta} = 1$ is $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}},$ then the sum of all the possible values of $\theta$ is (where, $\theta \in \left(0, \pi\right))$
questions.solution:
$e^{2} = 1 + \dfrac{\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta}{\left(1 + sin ⁡ \theta\right)2} = \dfrac{4}{3} ⇒ \dfrac{\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta}{\left(1 + sin ⁡ \theta\right)2} = \dfrac{1}{3}$
$⇒ \left[\dfrac{cos ⁡ \theta}{1 + sin ⁡ \theta}\right]2 = \dfrac{1}{3} ⇒ \left[\dfrac{sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)}{1 + cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)}\right]2 = \dfrac{1}{3}$
$⇒ \tan^{2} ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$
$\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{θ}{2} = \dfrac{- \pi}{6}, \dfrac{\pi}{6} ⇒ \dfrac{θ}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{6}, \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{6}$
$\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \pm \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}, \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$

Hence, the required sum $= \pi$

questions.q: From a point $P,$ tangents are drawn to the curve $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - {y}^{2} = 1 .$ If the chord of contact is a normal chord and the locus of $P$ is the curve $\dfrac{8}{{x}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{y}^{2}} = 10\lambda,$ then the value of $\lambda$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $P\left(h, k\right)$, then equation of chord of contact is $\dfrac{hx}{2} - ky = 1 \ldots \ldots \left(i\right)$
And equation of normal to hyperbola is $\sqrt{2}xcos ⁡ ϕ + ycot ⁡ ϕ = 3 \ldots \ldots \left(ii\right)$
On comparing $\left(i\right)$ and $\left(ii\right)$ , we get,
$cot ⁡ ϕ = - 3k, sec ⁡ ϕ = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3h}$
Now eliminating $ϕ,$ we get,
$\dfrac{8}{{h}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{k}^{2}} = 9 ∴ \lambda = 0.9$

questions.q: The tangent drawn to the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{16} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{9} = 1,$ at point $P$ in the first quadrant whose abscissa is $5,$ meets the lines $3x - 4y = 0$ and $3x + 4y = 0$ at $Q$ and $R$ respectively. If $O$ is the origin, then the area of triangle $OQR$ is (in square units)
questions.solution:
Let point $P$ be $\left(5, \beta\right)$ since it lies on given hyperbola $\dfrac{25}{16} - \dfrac{{\beta}^{2}}{9} = 1 ⇒ {\beta}^{2} = \dfrac{81}{16}$
Hence, $\beta = \dfrac{9}{4}$ (as $P$ lies in first quadrant)
So, equation of tangent is $\dfrac{5x}{16} - \dfrac{9y}{4 ⋅ 9} = 1 ⇒ 5x - 4y = 16$
So, points~$Q and R$ are $\left(8, 6\right)$ and $\left(2, - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)$
Hence, the area of triangle $OQR$ is $\dfrac{1}{2}\left(12 + 12\right) = 12$ sq. units

questions.q: Let the variable line $y = kx + h$ is tangent to the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{4} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{9} = 1 .$ If the locus of $P  \left(h, k\right) is a conic, then which of the following statement is false about this conic?$
options: Vertices of conic lies on y-axis
The eccentricity of conic is greater than the eccentricity of given hyperbola.
The centre of conic is at the origin
questions.solution:
Equation of the tangent $y = kx + h$ is compared with $y = mx \pm \sqrt{4m^{2} - 9}$
$⇒ 1 = \dfrac{m}{k} = \dfrac{\pm \sqrt{4m^{2} - 9}}{h}$
i.e. $m = k$ and $h = \sqrt{4m^{2} - 9}$
$⇒ h = \sqrt{4k^{2} - 9}$
$⇒ 4y^{2} - x^{2} = 9$
$⇒ \dfrac{{\text{y}^{2}}{{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{2}} - \dfrac{{\text{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}} = 1$
$⇒ {3}^{2} = {\$ left($\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$}^{2} $\left({\text{e}^{2} -1\right)$
$⇒ e^{2} = 5 ⇒ e = \sqrt{5}$> 1$

Hence, the conic is not an ellipse

$$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the line $2x + \sqrt{6}y = 2$ touches the hyperbola ${x}^{2} - 2{y}^{2} = {a}^{2},$ then ${a}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
The tangent to the hyperbola is $y = - \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{6}}x + \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{6}}$

Also, tangent to hyperbola in slope form is $y = mx \pm \sqrt{{a}^{2}{m}^{2} - {b}^{2}}$

i.e. $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{{a}^{2}{\left(\dfrac{- 2}{\sqrt{6}}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{2}}$

On squaring, we get,
$\dfrac{4}{6} = {a}^{2} ⋅ \dfrac{4}{6} - \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{2} ⇒ \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{6} ⇒ {a}^{2} = 4$
questions.question: If the line $2x + \sqrt{6}y = 2$ touches the hyperbola ${x}^{2} - 2{y}^{2} = {a}^{2},$ then ${a}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.explanation:

Also, tangent to hyperbola in slope form is $y = mx \pm \sqrt{{a}^{2}{m}^{2} - {b}^{2}}$

i.e. $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{{a}^{2}{\left(\dfrac{- 2}{\sqrt{6}}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{2}}$

On squaring, we get,
$\dfrac{4}{6} = {a}^{2} ⋅ \dfrac{4}{6} - \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{2} ⇒ \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{6} ⇒ {a}^{2} = 4$
